nearbyCountiesFullText.nwsHeadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EST WEDNESDAY
nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM this evening to 10 AM EST Wednesday.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued due to
stagnant conditions and calm winds. Fine particulate levels are
expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active
children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as
asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

000
FXUS63 KIWX 180742
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
242 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Temps lean above normal with sunshine through the rest of the
  week.

- After our dry spell this week, rain chances return Saturday
  night into Sunday (30-60% chance).

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 235 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

Surface high pressure just east of the Ohio River Valley and mid 
level ridging passing from the Plains States to the Mid Atlantic 
States is in control of the short term's weather providing dry 
conditions through late Saturday night. With high pressure to 
our east, modest WAA allows high temps to slowly warm between 
today and Friday so that all areas are securely in the 60s. Lows
stay above freezing and this will continue to be the case into 
the first half next week. We'll also have some breezy winds 
Thursday around 20 to 25 mph.

Temperatures drop Sunday as the moisture column becomes more 
saturated. A theta-e plume with connection to the Gulf swings 
through the area with PWAT standardized anomalies over 2. Even 
still, the arrival of the front will need to be watched because with 
its early arrival in the midday to early afternoon, maximum heating 
and instability formation is likely to be stunted limiting 
thunderstorm potential. Therefore, precipitation is expected to 
total 0.1" to 0.25" across the area with the highest residing in the 
southeast portion of the area. Behind this cold front, high temps 
will drop through the 50s and level out in the 40s the next work 
week with below freezing lows back in the picture for the end of 
next week. This is as 850 mb temperatures fall below 0C and the -10C 
contour gets near the area late Monday. Instability is generated on 
Monday as an area of cold air moves over the warmer lakes/ground, 
but the lake induced instability is fairly modest and the moisture 
column is rather dry. Low level lapse rates approach dry adiabatic 
though.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 1246 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

VFR conditions are expected at the terminals, with high clouds
and light south-southwesterly flow through the period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Air Quality Alert until 10 AM EST this morning for INZ005.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Roller
AVIATION...MCD

spc.text:
SPC AC 180545

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1145 PM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

   Valid 181200Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. today and
   tonight.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   A mid-level shortwave trough will move through the central U.S.
   today, as an upper-level low remains over the northeast Gulf. In the
   southern part of this system, scattered thunderstorms will be
   possible over much of the eastern Gulf extending eastward across the
   Florida Peninsula. Out west, an upper-level low will move toward the
   West Coast today. On the southern edge of the system, strong
   large-scale ascent will be favorable for isolated to scattered
   thunderstorms over much of central and northern California.

   No severe threat is forecast across the continental U.S. today or
   tonight.

   ..Broyles/Chalmers.. 11/18/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 180659

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1259 AM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

   Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE
   CENTRAL VALLEY OF CALIFORNIA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms are possible over portions
   of California with damaging gusts and a brief tornado possible.
   Additional non-severe storms are possible across the Great Basin,
   and into the Southeast Thursday and Thursday night.

   ...CA Central Valley...
   A deep upper low and embedded shortwave will move inland over the
   northern/central CA coast early Thursday. Attendant to the upper
   low, very strong westerly flow aloft will overspread a modestly
   moist air mass (dewpoints in the upper 40s to low 50s F) south of a
   weak surface low over the Central Valley. A narrow convective band
   is forecast to move inland during the morning with modest clearing
   in its wake. Mid-level temperatures near -25C will steepen lapse
   rates (7-7.5 C/km) amid weak diurnal heating, supporting
   destabilization with MLCAPE of 250-500 J/kg through the lowest 6-7
   km. 

   Concurrent with the shallow unstable profiles, terrain-enhanced
   southerly winds are expected across the valley. Elongated and
   modestly curved hodographs may support some stronger storms in the
   form of organized low-topped clusters or transient supercells. A
   low-end risk for damaging gusts and perhaps a brief tornado is
   possible across parts of the Central Valley through the morning and
   early afternoon. Thereafter, the arrival of the surface cold front
   and veering  winds will favor cooler surface temperatures and
   weakening buoyancy.

   Farther northeast into the Great Basin, more limited surface
   moisture is forecast across NV and western UT. Strong ascent from
   the approaching upper low will still support modest buoyancy
   favoring scattered thunderstorms. However, the weak buoyancy should
   preclude much severe risk.

   ...Southeast...
   A weak upper low over the Gulf will continue to diminish as diffuse
   surface cyclones moves from the central Gulf and off the eastern FL
   coast. Strengthening low-level flow will continue to promote
   isolated to perhaps scattered thunderstorms across the region. Weak
   flow aloft through much of the CAPE-bearing layer will limit the
   potential for severe convection, but sporadic gusts remain possible.

   ..Lyons.. 11/18/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 180830

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

   Valid 201200Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Friday.

   ...Central/Northern Rockies and Plains States...
   An upper trough over the Great basin is forecast to eject eastward
   across the Rockies and into the northern/central Plains as it merges
   with a second weaker perturbation emanating from southern Canada.
   Strong southwesterly flow aloft will overspread the Plains states
   deepening a lee cyclone across eastern CO/WY. This will draw modest
   surface moisture northward ahead of a cold front/lee trough tied to
   the low. Strong ascent ahead of the aforementioned trough and
   boundaries, along with the modest moisture return may support
   isolated thunderstorms across the Plains late Friday afternoon into
   early Saturday. While deep-layer flow will strengthen through the
   day, relatively cool surface temperatures and overall modest
   buoyancy suggests severe potential will be quite limited. Additional
   isolated storms are possible under the core of the upper trough
   throughout the higher terrain.

   ...Gulf and Atlantic Coasts...
   A weak upper trough will move from the eastern Gulf across the FL
   peninsula Friday. A broad low over open waters farther west should
   gradually fill while a compact secondary surface low is forecast to
   deepen along the Atlantic coast. Weak ascent fro the upper trough
   will support scattered thunderstorms within a moist and broad yet
   weakly unstable environment from the middle Gulf Coast to FL. Poor
   lapse rates and generally weak upper-level flow should preclude much
   in the way of storm organization. However, given scattered storm
   coverage, sporadic damaging gusts is possible.

   ..Lyons.. 11/18/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
